# Setting Up an Outlook Rule to Delay Sending Email

Here's how to create a rule that delays all outgoing emails:

## Method 1: Using Rules (Delays All Emails)

1. Open **Outlook**
2. Go to **File** → **Manage Rules & Alerts**
3. Click **New Rule**
4. Under "Start from a blank rule," select **Apply rule on messages I send**
5. Click **Next**
6. On the conditions screen, you can leave everything unchecked to apply to all messages (click **Yes** when prompted to confirm applying to all messages sent)
7. Click **Next**
8. Check the box for **"defer delivery by a number of minutes"**
9. Click the underlined **"a number of"** link
10. Enter the delay time (e.g., 1–120 minutes)
11. Click **OK**, then **Next**
12. Add any exceptions if needed (optional)
13. Name your rule (e.g., "Delay Send")
14. Click **Finish**

## Method 2: Delay a Single Email (Manual Option)

If you don't want a rule for every email:

1. Compose your email
2. Click **Options** tab
3. Select **Delay Delivery**
4. Set the desired **date/time** for sending
5. Click **Close**, then **Send**

The email will sit in your **Outbox** until the scheduled time.

## Important Notes

- The delay rule only works while **Outlook is open** — if you close Outlook before the delay period ends, the email won't send until you reopen it.
- Emails sit in the **Outbox** during the delay period, so don't disable your rule if you need to send something urgently — you can right-click the email in the Outbox and choose to send it immediately.
- This works differently in **Outlook.com/Outlook on the web**, where the interface may vary slightly.
